text:
Recent work supports separating multiple interests from candidate-dependent matching. [MARS (CIKM 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00702) constructs multiple attribute-aware user/item representations and scores their attribute-wise interactions, directly addressing complex preferences that a single pooled vector can obscure. Its pretrained-language-model setting does not establish effectiveness with catalog-only, randomly initialized text embeddings. [D2MFRec](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-31190-z) provides a complementary mechanism: target-item attention over multiple interest vectors, combined with a gated single-interest representation. Its ablations remove interest and denoising components; they do not isolate text grounding from additional capacity.

Pretraining assumptions require careful checking. The authors’ [RecSys 2024 implementation, The Elephant in the Room](https://github.com/777pomingzi/Rethinking-PLM-in-RS), explicitly downloads Longformer even under instructions called “pre-training from scratch”; that recipe violates the present weight restriction. The searched literature supplies useful architectural precedents, but no verified result establishing the exact combination of lightweight candidate-conditioned interests and catalog-only text learning under this Amazon protocol.

A practical hypothesis is to fuse item-ID embeddings with a small, randomly initialized token-embedding encoder over supplied titles/descriptions; extract 2–4 history interests using learned attention queries; let each candidate attend over those interests. Retain the SASRec final-state score through a learned residual gate. Train everything jointly on next-item prediction and cache catalog text representations for evaluation. To distinguish grounding from capacity, compare parameter-matched ID-only multi-interest, text plus single-interest, text plus multi-interest without candidate conditioning, and the complete model; add shuffled item–text assignments as a grounding control. Select using the prescribed four-category macro validation HR@10; these are proposed experiments, not demonstrated benchmark gains.
